prediction.likelyOutcome: GSA is more likely than not to prevail on the central factual question (Full Assessment occurred in 2015, not 2013/2014), meaning the Contracting Officer's $3,413,275.92 recoupment and the rent withholding would be sustained and GBA Associates would recover little to nothing on its breach claim; Plaintiff's alternative post-trial 'windfall damages' theory is unlikely to independently produce recovery. There is a real, non-trivial chance (not better than even) that the court instead finds 2013 or 2014 was the true Full Assessment year, in which case Plaintiff should recover the full withheld amount plus interest.

Summary Judgment Ruling Foreclosing Bilateral-Agreement/Estoppel Theory

outcome.description: After a five-day bench trial the court found that Fairfax County did not assess the Property taking into account all lease-contemplated renovations until tax year 2015, so GSA properly reestablished the Real Estate Tax Base at the 2015 bill ($1,993,293.46) and did not breach the Lease by withholding rent to recoup its claimed $3.4 million of excess tax adjustments; it also declined the lessor's post-trial windfall-damages theory (that the County should have used the cost approach in 2015). Judgment was directed for the United States; the lessor recovered nothing. No appeal is reflected in the opinion.
outcome.finalNote: Defense judgment. No appeal reflected in the opinion text (subsequent history not otherwise checked). The opinion states no dollar demand by the lessor; its economic stake is the roughly $3.4 million GSA recouped by withholding rent.
